data.name: Chakradhar
data.gender_notes: Chakradhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chakradhar is derived from Sanskrit words 'Chakra' meaning wheel and 'Dhar' meaning holder. This name is bestowed upon individuals believed to hold the wheel of life or power in their hands. The name Chakradhar carries the meaning “Holder of the wheel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chakradhar usually hope their child will grow to embody holder of the wheel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power to control the cycle of life and the universe.
data.etymology: Chakradhar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Holder of the wheel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chakradhar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu is often depicted riding a celestial chariot, and Chakra, a discus, is one of his primary weapons. Wielding this symbol of power, Lord Vishnu maintains the balance of the universe, preserving dharma. As Chakradhar, a person embodies the strength, power and control associated with this divine entity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Chakradhar holds deep spiritual significance as it reflects the belief in the cyclical nature of life and existence. It emphasizes the journey of the soul, who is the true holder, riding the wheel of life. A person named Chakradhar is considered blessed with the power and wisdom to guide others in their spiritual journey towards self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chakradhar: The one who holds the wheel of time and cosmic energies, symbolizing control over the cycles of life and the universe.

historical_references.reference: Chakradhar Swami was a prominent Jain monk and scholar, who contributed significantly to Jain literature during the 12th and 13th centuries. He is known for his work 'Dharmamarmacaritrasataka', which is a collection of 108 beautiful and inspiring stories that illustrate Jain moral values.

Another Chakradhar, also known as Chakradhar Samhita, was a celebrated Hindu saint and poet, who lived during the 16th century. He is famous for his work 'Chakradhar Samhita', which is a comprehensive text on classical Indian music and dance, specifically on the Mohana and Bhairava ragas.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Chakradhar' is derived from Hindu mythology, where Chakra represents a discus weapon and Dhar means holder. In modern context, this name is popularly used among technology enthusiasts and spiritual individuals. On Twitter, hashtags like #ChakradharTech or #ChakradharSpirituality are common, where discussions revolve around the latest technology trends and spiritual practices. Instagram is another platform where users with this name share their personal journeys of integrating technology with spirituality, showcasing their yoga practices, tech gadgets, and inspirational quotes. Lastly, on YouTube, channels named 'Chakradhar' offer a blend of technology tutorials, spiritual content, and motivational speeches, appealing to a wide audience seeking knowledge and spiritual growth.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Chakradhar, a teacher in Bangalore, India, shares that their name Chakradhar meaning "Holder of the wheel" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
